subject_identity_derivation.supersedes: RCO_CLOSURE_DIGEST_V2 (v1.0.4). Differences, and nothing else: (1) the import grammar is anchored to import/export STATEMENTS, so an import-shaped string inside a test fixture is not an import (the v1.0.4 test holds such a string, which made the package kind underivable); (2) the runtime literal grammar admits one or more "./" or "../" segments (RNB-LIT); (3) absent_reference_policy per kind; (4) every file set is named by role (RNB-S4). KS-A and KS-B recompute to their v1.0.4 package digests.
steps: S1 C must name a COMMIT object; tree_sha = C^{tree}; tree_sha never equals candidate_sha.
S2 COVERED = every path of the tree of C starting with a covered_path_prefix of the kind, byte-sorted, non-empty.

S3 IMPORTED = transitive closure over repository imports. Scanned files: the COVERED paths matching grammars.code_file, then every newly IMPORTED path matching grammars.code_file. In each scanned file (comments NOT removed) every match of grammars.import_specifier (flags g and m) yields the first non-empty capture group as the specifier. A specifier starting with "." resolves against the directory of the scanned file, one starting with "@/" against the repository root; others (packages, node: builtins) are not followed. Resolution tries import_resolution_suffixes in order; the first existing path wins; none existing fails the derivation.

S4 TOOLCHAIN = the kind's toolchain_roots (each must exist at C), plus every quoted string inside the brackets of each grammars.setup_files match in a toolchain root matching grammars.code_file (resolved against that root's directory; must exist), plus the S3 closure seeded with exactly those toolchain paths, labelled TOOLCHAIN. A path already assigned a role keeps it.

S5 RUNTIME_INPUT = for each COVERED path matching grammars.code_file (and ONLY those: not TOOLCHAIN, not IMPORTED), its text with grammars.block_comment matches removed and then grammars.line_comment matches replaced by their first group, scanned with grammars.runtime_literal (flag g); a capture starting with "." resolves against the file directory, any other against the repository root; the result is RUNTIME_INPUT if it exists at C, is not already assigned and does not match docs/ops/**.json. Captures that name no existing path are ignored (output paths, globs, identifiers). RUNTIME_INPUT files are never scanned further.

S6 GOVERNING = every distinct match of grammars.governing_reference in the full text (comments included) of every COVERED, TOOLCHAIN and IMPORTED path (not RUNTIME_INPUT), in byte order, not already assigned. An absent path follows the kind's absent_reference_policy.
S7 entries = COVERED, TOOLCHAIN, IMPORTED, RUNTIME_INPUT, GOVERNING, each byte-sorted by path, as {role, path, blob}.
S8 package_digest = lowercase hex sha256 over the UTF-8 concatenation of role TAB path TAB blob LF for each entry in order.

S9 governing_families = distinct prefixes of the GOVERNING paths up to and including the character before the first "_v<digit>" (the whole path when absent), byte-sorted; governing_family_members_at_candidate = every path of the tree of C starting with a family, byte-sorted, with its blob.

git_read_environment.rule: EVERY git read whose result a consumer or materializer relies on (history, tree listing, blob bytes, ancestry, shallow and object-format checks) runs in the controlled environment below. environment.construction: Built from NOTHING, never by copying and filtering the parent environment (a case-sensitive deny-list is bypassable on Windows). Copied from the parent: PATH, SystemRoot, TEMP, TMP (only what the platform needs to start git). Set: HOME, USERPROFILE and XDG_CONFIG_HOME to a fresh private directory; GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1; GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=an empty file in that directory; GIT_NO_REPLACE_OBJECTS=1; GIT_GRAFT_FILE=a path inside a fresh private directory, checked ABSENT before every read; GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1; GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0; GIT_PAGER=cat; GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0. Nothing else: in particular no inherited GIT_DIR, GIT_WORK_TREE, GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY, GIT_ALTERNATE_OBJECT_DIRECTORIES, GIT_NAMESPACE, GIT_REPLACE_REF_BASE, GIT_SHALLOW_FILE, GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS, GIT_CONFIG_COUNT/KEY/VALUE or GIT_INDEX_FILE.

git_read_environment.self_check: Before relying on any read: (a) git config --list --show-scope under the environment lists no system or global scope entry; (b) for every pinned key, the effective value is the pinned value (command-line scope wins over repository and included configuration); (c) no fsck.* key is effective (defence in depth for object_integrity); (d) git rev-parse --show-object-format prints sha1; (e) the graft path is absent. object_integrity.rule: Pre-commit review B1. git does NOT re-hash an object on ordinary reads (parent walk, ls-tree, cat-file --batch): a loose object rewritten in place under its original id, a forged pack index or multi-pack-index, or an alternate object store can change what a commit, tree or blob says while every id stays the same. Therefore, before any other read, git fsck --full --no-dangling --no-progress runs under the controlled environment and must exit 0 (it re-hashes every loose and packed object, including alternates, and verifies pack indexes). Any error: STOP_GIT_OBJECT_STORE_CORRUPT.

ever_added_history.rule: R3-1: let U be the union of every path under the adjudication root that was ever ADDED in the FULL reachable history of the consumer head H (which contains the canonical tip and the store genesis). EVERY path in U: (1) is present at H; (2) has at H the blob that its single ADD introduced; (3) has exactly ONE add entry, in a non-merge commit, with mode 100644; (4) has ZERO modify, delete, type-change, rename or copy entries; (5) has ZERO merge (combined) entries; and (6) passes store_integrity at H. Conversely every path under the root at H is in U. Violations are root-wide.
ever_added_history.revision: Pre-commit review B2: the walk names H explicitly (the draft walked the checkout HEAD, so a consumer evaluating H while its checkout stood on an older commit could miss a merge drop in H). The file listing is git ls-tree -r -z --full-tree <H> -- <adjudication_root>. History and listing therefore describe the same commit, independently of the checkout and of the working directory.
ever_added_history.parse: Records start with \x01 followed by the commit and its parents; a non-merge entry is ":<src mode> <dst mode> <src oid> <dst oid> <status>" NUL <path> NUL; a merge (combined) entry starts with "::" (one mode and oid per parent plus the result) NUL <path> NUL.
ever_added_history.why: v1.0.4 checked only paths PRESENT at H: a record dropped by a merge (-s ours, or a normal merge resolving it away) leaves no delete and no combined entry, so it vanished silently (RB-1). A path that was ever added is never allowed to be absent or different at H, whatever the merge did. --full-history walks every parent of every merge, so the side commit that added the dropped record is always listed.
ever_added_history.proven_against: companion test, real DAGs: merge -s ours drop, normal merge then git rm, evil merge, add/add on two branches, delete and restart, rename, modify, legitimate side-branch add merged normally, root-commit add, forged commit-graph, replace (log and ls-tree), info/grafts, shallow clone, local log.showRoot=false.

Immediately before evaluation the consumer obtains, from the PROVIDER (GitHub REST, read-only), the tip of CANONICAL_ADJUDICATION_REF (never from a local ref, which local history rewrites can move) and the protection facts of provider_protection. It then requires, with controlled reads: (a) the provider-observed ref name equals CANONICAL_ADJUDICATION_REF; (b) STORE_GENESIS is an ancestor of (or equal to) the provider tip; (c) for EVERY RECERT_ATTEMPT at H, its canonical_store.tip_observed_at_reservation is an ancestor of (or equal to) the provider tip, so the canonical history never moved backwards past a reservation; (d) the provider tip is an ancestor of (or equal to) H, so the canonical history, including any record ever added on it, is inside the history ever_added_history inspects; (e) provider_protection evaluates PASS; (f) the provider activity witness shows no force_push and no branch_deletion of the ref. (b) or (c) failing: STOP_CANONICAL_STORE_NOT_MONOTONIC. (d): STOP_ADJUDICATION_STORE_STALE. (e): STOP_PROVIDER_PROTECTION_REQUIRED. (f): STOP_CANONICAL_STORE_REWRITTEN. provider_protection.activity_witness: GET repos/{o}/{r}/activity?ref=<CANONICAL_ADJUDICATION_REF>, read through EVERY page, lists no entry with activity_type force_push or branch_deletion and at most ONE branch_creation (a second creation means the ref was deleted or renamed away and recreated). A supplementary witness only: it is NOT sufficient without protection (its retention is the provider's), and it is necessary so that a rewrite that happened while protection was off is not ignored when it is still visible.

why_no_repository_only_substitute: A pin of the "last governed tip" written into the repository lives inside the very ref it is meant to protect: a force-push replaces the pin together with the history it pins.

A FAIL materialized and then removed by a force-push between two observations leaves no reachable object: git content cannot prove that an unreachable commit never existed (owner v1.0.3), and no clone is obliged to have fetched it.
Attempt records carry tip_observed_at_reservation, but they are themselves in the rewritable ref; they detect a rewrite only when they survive it.
Local reflogs, other clones and CI caches are not governed, not complete and not shared; treating them as the store would make the result depend on which machine evaluates.
Therefore the only sound guarantee is the provider refusing the rewrite: a ruleset (or classic protection) on the canonical ref, read back read-only by every consumer.

attempt_contract.rule: Owner v1.0.3. Every governed independent recertification of any subject kind has exactly one RECERT_ATTEMPT, materialized on the canonical ref by a reservation lane BEFORE the review begins, and resolved by exactly one ADJUDICATION of any verdict class, materialized by a separate lane. An adjudication without an attempt is invalid. An independent report outside the repository is not consumable; while its attempt is unresolved every positive certification of that package_digest is suspended (STOP_RECERT_ATTEMPT_OPEN).
